newsitem.title: CYPRUS: UN envoy due in Cyprus next week for talks.
newsitem.headline: UN envoy due in Cyprus next week for talks.

text.p: The United Nations special envoy for Cyprus Han Sung-joo will visit the island on April 12 to push for talks between rival sides on the divided island, a U.N. spokesman said on Friday.

"The visit is to reinforce our efforts aimed at getting both leaders together, preferably before the middle of the year," said Waldemar Rokoszewski, spokesman for the U.N. force stationed on the island.
Han, appointed special representative of the U.N. secretary-general in May 1996, will stay in Cyprus for about a week before travelling on to Athens and Ankara, Rokoszewski said.
Leaders of Cyprus's Greek and Turkish communities, divided since Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974 after a coup sponsored by Athens, have not met since October 1994.

United Nations permanent representative Gustave Feissel started proximity talks between the two sides in early March in preparation of direct talks which could take place between leaders Glafcos Clerides and Rauf Denktash.

Clerides is president of the administration in the south, internationally recognised as the island's only legitimate government. Denktash heads a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north recognised only by Ankara.
United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan will meet Denktash in Geneva next week.

The U.N. has indicated it wants to see both sides make "goodwill gestures" to the other to improve the climate for talks, soured after the killings of three Greek Cypriots on the ceasefire line by Turks or Turkish Cypriots, and the shooting of a Turkish Cypriot sentry between August and October last year.
The U.N. have a force of 1,200 patrolling a buffer zone between some 30,000 mainland Turkish forces in northern Cyprus and 11,500 Greek Cypriot conscripts in the south.
